HKD-001.q: From the 2026 tax period, a household business does NOT pay VAT and PIT when annual revenue is:
HKD-001.e: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP amending Decree 68/2026/ND-CP raised the threshold to VND 1 billion per year.
HKD-001.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (amended by Decree 141/2026/ND-CP); Law 09/2026/QH16.
Analysis: From 2026, household businesses with annual revenue ≤ 1 billion pay no VAT or PIT. The threshold uses total revenue across all locations (HKD-003).
Distractors: 500 million was Decree 68/2026's original level; 100 million is a pre-2025 threshold; 3 billion is a method grouping point.

HKD-002.q: The VND 1 billion threshold was raised by Decree 141/2026/ND-CP from the VND 500 million originally set in Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
HKD-002.e: True. VND 500 million per year was raised to VND 1 billion per year.
HKD-002.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Decree 68/2026 originally set 500 million/year; after Law 09/2026 delegated the threshold, Decree 141/2026 raised it to 1 billion/year from the 2026 period.

HKD-003.q: A household business with several locations applies the VND 1 billion threshold to total revenue of all locations, and the VND 1 billion is deducted only once.
HKD-003.e: True. Locations cannot be split so each enjoys its own threshold.
HKD-003.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 1 billion threshold applies to the household's total revenue (all locations and lines) and is deducted only once – preventing location splitting to multiply the threshold (HKD-004).

HKD-004.q: A household business with two shops, each with revenue of VND 600 million per year, pays no VAT or PIT because each shop is below VND 1 billion.
HKD-004.e: False. Total revenue of VND 1.2 billion exceeds the threshold, so tax is payable.
HKD-004.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Total revenue = 600 + 600 = 1.2 billion > 1 billion → VAT on full revenue and PIT (percentage method) on the excess over 1 billion, or under the income method.

HKD-005.q: Select ALL correct statements for a household business with annual revenue above VND 1 billion up to 3 billion:
HKD-005.e: Household businesses pay PIT, not CIT.
o: May choose PIT at a % rate on revenue exceeding VND 1 billion
May choose PIT under the income method at 15%
VAT is computed at a % rate on revenue
HKD-005.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP; Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: The above-1-to-3-billion group: (A) may choose PIT as a percentage of revenue above 1 billion; (B) or the income method at 15%; (C) VAT is always a percentage of revenue.
Distractors: (D) Household businesses aren't CIT taxpayers (CIT-127).

HKD-006.q: A household business with annual revenue above VND 3 billion up to 50 billion computes PIT as:
HKD-006.e: Above VND 50 billion the rate is 20%.
o: Lump-sum tax set by the tax authority
HKD-006.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Above 3 to 50 billion: PIT = (revenue − reasonable costs) × 17%, the income method being mandatory. Above 50 billion: 20%.
Distractors: B is the percentage method (not available here); C is for above 50 billion; D – presumptive tax has ended.

HKD-007.q: Match each household business revenue band with its PIT method:
HKD-007.e: Four revenue bands determine the PIT method.
p: Choose % on revenue above 1 billion, or income × 15%
HKD-007.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Four groups: ≤ 1 billion – no VAT/PIT; > 1–3 billion – percentage on the excess over 1 billion or income × 15%; > 3–50 billion – income × 17%; > 50 billion – income × 20%. The rates mirror small-company CIT (15%/17%/20%).

HKD-008.q: A household business with annual revenue above VND 3 billion cannot choose to compute PIT at a % rate on revenue.
HKD-008.e: True. The above-3-billion band must use the income method (revenue − expenses).
HKD-008.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Household businesses above 3 billion must use the income method (revenue − costs), requiring books and documents – close to company obligations.

HKD-009.q: Once revenue exceeds the threshold, the VND 1 billion deduction applies only to PIT at % rates; VAT is computed on total revenue.
HKD-009.e: True. E.g., retail of 2 billion: VAT = 2 billion × 1% = 20 million; PIT = (2 − 1) billion × 0.5% = 5 million.
HKD-009.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 1 billion deduction applies only to percentage-method PIT; VAT is on full revenue. E.g., 2 billion retail: VAT = 2,000 × 1% = 20 million; PIT = (2,000 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 5 million.

HKD-010.q: VAT of a household business above the threshold is computed by:
HKD-010.e: Household businesses do not claim input VAT; the % depends on the activity.
o: Input tax credit like an enterprise
HKD-010.x:
Basis: VAT Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Household businesses above the threshold pay VAT as a percentage of revenue (direct method, VAT-060), without input credits; rates vary by sector.
Distractors: B is for enterprises (VAT-067); C is for gold and silver; D is abolished.

HKD-011.q: Household businesses that paid lump-sum tax before 2026 are not back-taxed for differences when switching to self-declaration, except where revenue was concealed or fraud occurred.
HKD-011.e: True. The transition policy encourages transparency without retroactive collection.
HKD-011.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Households that paid presumptive tax before 2026 aren't reassessed for the difference when switching to self-declaration – encouraging transparency; the exception is concealment or fraud.

HKD-012.q: A household business newly registered in 2026 must still pay business licence fee for its first year.
HKD-012.e: False. The business licence fee was abolished from 01/01/2026 under Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
HKD-012.x:
Basis: Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: False. The licence fee was abolished from 01/01/2026 for everyone, including household businesses registered in 2026.

HKD-013.q: Select ALL items included in a household business's taxable revenue:
HKD-013.e: Loans and capital contributions are not revenue.
o: Proceeds from selling goods and services
Bonuses, volume rebates and trade discounts received from suppliers
HKD-013.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Taxable revenue includes (A) sales of goods and services; (B) volume bonuses, support and trade discounts from suppliers (business income in substance); (C) surcharges kept.
Distractors: (D) loans and (E) capital contributions are funding, not revenue.

HKD-014.q: An individual leasing a house with revenue of VND 900 million per year:
HKD-014.e: Revenue not exceeding VND 1 billion per year is not taxable.
o: Pays 5% VAT and 5% PIT on total revenue
HKD-014.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Rental revenue of 900 million ≤ 1 billion → no VAT or PIT. (Above the threshold: VAT 5%, PIT 5% – PIT-110.)
Distractors: B and C apply above the threshold; D – presumptive tax has ended.

HKD-015.q: As of 19/10/2026, the PIT rule for household businesses with revenue above VND 3 billion:
HKD-015.e: The Tax Department (16/10/2026) said the MOF is reporting to competent authorities on an amendment; no replacement text yet.
o: Still follows the current income method; amendment is only at the MOF proposal stage
HKD-015.x:
Basis: Tax Department statement of 16/10/2026; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: As of 19/10/2026, changing PIT for households above 3 billion is only a Ministry of Finance proposal; the current income method still applies (ADM-111).
Distractors: B, C and D describe changes with no legal text.

HKD-016.q: When a household business's cumulative revenue in the year exceeds VND 1 billion, it:
HKD-016.e: It registers for e-invoices within 30 days from the last day of the period in which cumulative revenue exceeds VND 1 billion.
o: Switches to quarterly filing from the quarter in which the threshold is exceeded and uses e-invoices
Must immediately convert into an enterprise
HKD-016.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Once cumulative revenue exceeds 1 billion → file quarterly from that quarter; register for e-invoices within 30 days after the end of that period (ADM-064).
Distractors: B and C delay obligations; D – conversion to an enterprise isn't mandatory.

HKD-017.q: A household business with revenue of VND 1 billion or less pays no tax but must still notify its revenue to the tax authority.
HKD-017.e: True. Revenue data determine when the threshold is exceeded.
HKD-017.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Households ≤ 1 billion still report revenue (twice a year if operating from January – ADM-063) so the authority can monitor threshold breaches.

HKD-018.q: Consider these statements on 2026 household business tax policy:
HKD-018.e: Household businesses pay PIT, not CIT.
o: Household businesses determine their own revenue to declare and pay tax.
Household businesses pay CIT instead of PIT.
The non-taxable threshold is VND 1 billion per year.
HKD-018.x:
Basis: Resolution 198/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – presumptive tax ended 01/01/2026. (2) True – self-determined revenue. (3) False – households pay PIT, not CIT. (4) True – 1 billion/year threshold.

HKD-019.q: Match each activity group with the household business VAT rate on revenue:
HKD-019.e: VAT % rates reflect the average value added of each activity group.
p: Manufacturing, transport, food & beverage, construction with materials
HKD-019.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: VAT rates: goods distribution 1%; services and construction excluding materials 5%; production, transport, food service, construction including materials 3%; other 2% – reflecting average value added (like VAT-060).

HKD-020.q: Match each activity group with the PIT rate on revenue (portion above VND 1 billion):
HKD-020.e: Other activities: 1%; lottery, insurance and multi-level marketing agents: 5%.
HKD-020.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: PIT rates (on revenue above 1 billion): goods distribution 0.5%; services and construction excluding materials 2%; production, transport, food service 1.5%; asset leasing 5%; other 1%; lottery, insurance and multi-level agents 5%.

HKD-021.q: A household café or restaurant applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-021.e: Food & beverage belongs to the manufacturing, transport and goods-related services group.
HKD-021.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Cafés and eateries are food services – the production/transport/goods-related services group: VAT 3%, PIT 1.5%.
Distractors: B is goods distribution; C is pure services; D is 'other'.

HKD-022.q: A household hair salon applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-022.e: Services not tied to goods apply 5% VAT and 2% PIT.
HKD-022.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Hairdressing and beauty are services not tied to goods: VAT 5%, PIT 2%.
Distractors: B is food/production; C is distribution; D is 'other'.

HKD-023.q: A household contractor doing construction WITHOUT supplying materials applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-023.e: With materials supplied, the rates are 3% / 1.5%.
HKD-023.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Construction excluding materials is mainly labour – the services group: VAT 5%, PIT 2%. Including materials: 3% / 1.5% (HKD-024).
Distractors: B is with materials; C and D are wrong groups.

HKD-024.q: A household contractor doing construction WITH materials supplied applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-024.e: Construction with materials belongs to the 3% / 1.5% group.
HKD-024.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Construction including materials has a large materials share and lower value added → VAT 3% / PIT 1.5%.
Distractors: B is excluding materials; C is distribution; D has no basis.

HKD-025.q: A retail grocery store applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-025.e: Distribution and supply of goods has the lowest rates.
HKD-025.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Grocery retail is goods distribution – the lowest rates: VAT 1%, PIT 0.5%.
Distractors: B, C and D are higher value-added groups.

HKD-026.q: A household freight transport business applies 3% VAT and 1.5% PIT.
HKD-026.e: True. Transport belongs to the manufacturing, transport and goods-related services group.
HKD-026.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Freight transport is in the production/transport/goods-related group: VAT 3%, PIT 1.5%.

HKD-027.q: Household karaoke and massage services belong to the services group with 5% VAT and 2% PIT.
HKD-027.e: True. These are services not tied to goods.
HKD-027.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Karaoke and massage are services not tied to goods: VAT 5%, PIT 2%. (They also bear excise tax under separate law.)

HKD-028.q: A household business with several activities must declare revenue by rate group; if revenue per group cannot be determined, the highest group rate applies.
HKD-028.e: True. Separating revenue avoids applying the high rate to everything.
HKD-028.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Multi-line households must declare revenue by rate group; if not separable, the highest group rate applies to everything – so tracking revenue separately (e.g., a shop selling groceries and food) legitimately lowers tax.

HKD-029.q: A grocery store has 2026 revenue of VND 2.4 billion. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-029.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (tax on household and individual businesses – per the question).
Working: Goods distribution/supply: VAT rate 1% on total revenue: 2,400 × 1% = 24 million VND (the tax-free revenue threshold isn't deducted for VAT).
Analysis: Revenue of 2.4 billion exceeds the exempt threshold, so VAT applies to all revenue. PIT is computed separately under the rules for that revenue band.
Note: Decree 68/2026 is a 2026 text beyond my knowledge; the explanation follows the question's basis – check the original (especially how thresholds apply to VAT and PIT).

HKD-030.q: The same grocery store with revenue of VND 2.4 billion chooses the % method. What PIT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-030.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Percentage-method PIT on the excess over 1 billion: (2,400 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 7 million. Total tax = 24 (VAT – HKD-029) + 7 = 31 million VND.

HKD-031.q: Consider these statements on the % of revenue method:
HKD-031.e: The direct method has no input tax credit mechanism.
o: VAT is computed on total revenue.
PIT is computed on revenue exceeding VND 1 billion.
The household business may claim input VAT.
HKD-031.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – VAT on full revenue. (2) True – PIT on the excess over 1 billion. (3) False – the direct method has no input credit (HKD-034). (4) True – rates by sector.

HKD-032.q: Taxable revenue under the % method is revenue including tax (where taxable).
HKD-032.e: True. VAT is not separated from revenue before applying the rate.
HKD-032.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Under the percentage method, taxable revenue is the total amount collected (tax-inclusive); VAT isn't separated before applying the rate – unlike the enterprise credit method.

HKD-033.q: An individual acting as an insurance, lottery or multi-level marketing agent with commission above the threshold pays:
HKD-033.e: Commission from selling lottery, insurance and MLM at set prices is not subject to VAT at the agent level.
HKD-033.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Lottery, insurance and multi-level agents selling at set prices for commission: PIT 5% on commissions (above the threshold); no VAT on commissions at the agent stage (the principal accounts for VAT on the sale price).
Distractors: B and C apply inappropriate VAT rates; D is wrong above the threshold.

HKD-034.q: A household business paying under the % method cannot claim input VAT on purchases.
HKD-034.e: True. VAT is therefore a cost to the household business.
HKD-034.x:
Basis: VAT Law 48/2024/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The percentage method has no input credit; VAT paid on purchases is a cost for the household, included in cost of goods.

HKD-035.q: A restaurant has annual revenue of VND 1.8 billion. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-035.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (per the question); the category 'production, transport, services involving goods' (including food service).
Working: VAT rate 3% on total revenue: 1,800 × 3% = 54 million VND.
Analysis: Food service falls under services with goods (ingredients processed) → 3%, unlike pure services (5%, e.g., beauty – HKD-108) and goods distribution (1% – HKD-052). The right category determines the rate.
Note: A 2026 text – check the annexed activity list and rates in the original.

HKD-036.q: A restaurant with revenue of VND 1.8 billion chooses the % method. What PIT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-036.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: PIT = (1,800 − 1,000) × 1.5% = 12 million. Total tax = 54 + 12 = 66 million VND.

HKD-037.q: Select ALL activities in the 3% VAT / 1.5% PIT group:
HKD-037.e: House leasing: 5%/5%; brokerage is a service: 5%/2%.
HKD-037.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The 3% / 1.5% group: (A) confectionery production; (B) passenger transport; (C) food service.
Distractors: (D) House rental: VAT 5%, PIT 5%; (E) property brokerage is a service: 5% / 2%.

HKD-038.q: The % of revenue method does not require the household business to prove expenses to compute PIT.
HKD-038.e: True. It is simple, but can be disadvantageous when margins are thin.
HKD-038.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The percentage method needs no cost evidence – simple; but it can be unfavourable when actual margins are below the implied rate, or favourable when margins are high (HKD-049).

HKD-039.q: Under the income method, a household business's taxable income for PIT equals:
HKD-039.e: Expenses must have lawful invoices/documents and relate to the business.
HKD-039.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Income method: taxable income = revenue − reasonable business costs (with lawful invoices and documents).
Distractors: B is the percentage-method base; C is the percentage method; D isn't the legal definition.

HKD-040.q: A household business with revenue of VND 2.5 billion and reasonable expenses of 2.0 billion chooses the income method. What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-040.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 2.5 billion revenue (1–3 billion group) using the income method: (2,500 − 2,000) × 15% = 75 million VND.
Note: Compare with the percentage method in HKD-049.

HKD-041.q: A household business has revenue of VND 5 billion and reasonable expenses of 4.2 billion. What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-041.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 5 billion revenue (> 3–50 billion group) must use the income method: (5,000 − 4,200) × 17% = 136 million VND.

HKD-042.q: A household business has revenue of VND 60 billion and taxable income of 3 billion. What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-042.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (per the question) – large household businesses paying PIT on taxable income.
Working: Revenue of 60 billion (> 50 billion) → a 20% rate on taxable income: 3,000 × 20% = 600 million VND.
Analysis: For large households, tax shifts from a revenue percentage to income (revenue − deductible costs), like companies (20% matching the CIT rate for firms above 50 billion – CIT-137). It requires full books and cost documents.
Note: A 2026 text – check revenue thresholds and rates in the original.

HKD-043.q: Select ALL expenses NOT deductible under the income method:
HKD-043.e: Wages of hired employees with contracts and records are deductible.
o: Wages of the household owner and household members
Wages of employees with labour contracts and payment records
HKD-043.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-deductible: (A) non-business spending; (B) spending without lawful documents; (C) wages of the owner and household members (a distribution of income in substance); (D) administrative fines.
Distractors: (E) Wages of hired staff with contracts and records are deductible (HKD-055).

HKD-044.q: Wages the household owner pays to themselves are deductible expenses.
HKD-044.e: False. Wages of the owner and household members are not deductible.
HKD-044.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Wages the owner pays themselves just move money between pockets of the same taxpayer; they aren't a business cost and aren't deductible.

HKD-045.q: Depreciation of a passenger car registered to an individual and used for travel is not deductible, except for transport and tourism household businesses using it in business.
HKD-045.e: True. Likewise, residential houses and land registered to individuals cannot be depreciated as expenses.
HKD-045.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Cars in an individual's name used for travel are personal consumption, so depreciation isn't deductible; the exception is transport and tourism households using them directly. Likewise, residential houses and land in personal names can't be depreciated.

HKD-046.q: Which depreciation is deductible for a household business using the income method?
HKD-046.e: Assets used directly in the business and depreciated within limits are deductible.
o: A cargo truck used in the household's transport business
A car the owner uses for school runs
Depreciation in excess of the prescribed limit
HKD-046.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: A delivery truck used directly in the household's transport business, depreciated within limits → deductible.
Distractors: B and C are personal-use assets (HKD-045); D – excess depreciation isn't deductible (HKD-053).

HKD-047.q: A household business declares expenses of VND 2.2 billion, including owner's wages 240 million, administrative fines 20 million and expenses without invoices 100 million. What are deductible expenses (VND million)?
HKD-047.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Deductible = 2,200 − 240 (owner's wage) − 20 (fine) − 100 (no invoice) = 1,840 million VND.

HKD-048.q: A household business with annual revenue of VND 2.6 billion chooses the income method at 15%. Declared costs are 2.2 billion, including the owner's salary 240 million, administrative fines 20 million and undocumented spending 100 million (all non-deductible). What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-048.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Deductible costs = 2,200 − 240 − 20 − 100 = 1,840 million. Taxable income = 2,600 − 1,840 = 760 million. PIT = 760 × 15% = 114 million VND.
Note: Under the percentage method (e.g., retail 0.5%): (2,600 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 8 million – compare before choosing.

HKD-049.q: A retail shop has revenue of VND 2.5 billion and reasonable expenses of 2.0 billion. The more favourable PIT option is:
o: % method: VND 7.5 million (lower than the income method's 75 million)
HKD-049.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Percentage: (2,500 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 7.5 million. Income method: (2,500 − 2,000) × 15% = 75 million. The percentage method saves 67.5 million.
Note: For retail with a 20% margin the income method is usually worse; loss-making or very low-margin households may benefit from it.

HKD-050.q: A household business using the income method must keep accounting books of revenue and expenses and retain invoices and documents.
HKD-050.e: True. Without books and documents, expenses cannot be proven.
HKD-050.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC (household business accounting).
Analysis: True. The income method requires books of revenue and costs plus invoices and documents – without them, costs can't be proven and tax may be assessed (HKD-056).

HKD-051.q: A household business using the income method for PIT still computes VAT at a % rate on revenue.
HKD-051.e: True. The income method applies only to PIT.
HKD-051.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The income method applies only to PIT; household VAT is always a percentage of full revenue.

HKD-052.q: A goods distribution household business has revenue of VND 5 billion. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-052.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (per the question); the 'goods distribution/supply' category.
Working: VAT rate 1%: 5,000 × 1% = 50 million VND.
Analysis: Distribution has the lowest rate (1%) because trading adds little value. A 5-billion household must meet e-invoice and filing requirements under the new tax administration rules (moving from presumptive tax to self-declaration).
Note: A 2026 text – check the original.

HKD-053.q: Depreciation of fixed assets in excess of the prescribed limit is treated as:
HKD-053.e: Only depreciation within the prescribed limit is deductible.
o: Carried forward to the next year
HKD-053.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Depreciation above prescribed limits (useful-life bands, cost caps) isn't deductible; only the amount within limits is.
Distractors: B, C and D have no basis.

HKD-054.q: Consider these statements on the household business income method:
HKD-054.e: Wages of the owner and household members are not deductible.
o: Households with revenue above 1–3 billion may choose the 15% rate.
HKD-054.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – > 3–50 billion: 17%. (2) True – > 50 billion: 20%. (3) True – 1–3 billion may choose 15%. (4) False – the owner's wage isn't deductible (HKD-044).

HKD-055.q: Wages of hired employees with labour contracts and payment records are deductible.
HKD-055.e: True. Paying wages via bank transfer provides clear evidence.
HKD-055.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Wages of hired staff with employment contracts and payment records are deductible. Pay by bank transfer for clear evidence, and mind PIT withholding and social insurance duties.

HKD-056.q: A household business with revenue above VND 3 billion keeps no books and has no expense documents. The main risk is:
HKD-056.e: The Tax Administration Law allows tax assessment when the taxpayer keeps no books or cannot present documents.
o: The tax authority may impose (assess) the tax payable
It is automatically switched to the % method
HKD-056.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: A household above 3 billion without books or cost documents can't apply the income method; the authority may assess tax (ADM-081), usually unfavourably.
Distractors: B – there's no automatic switch; C and D misjudge the risk.

HKD-057.q: The deadline for a household business's quarterly tax return is:
HKD-057.e: The payment deadline coincides with the filing deadline.
o: The last day of the first month of the next quarter
The 20th of the first month of the next quarter
The last day of the quarter
HKD-057.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Quarterly filing is due by the last day of the next quarter's first month; payment is due the same day.
Distractors: B is the monthly deadline; C and D are wrong.

HKD-058.q: The household business filing deadline for Q3/2026 is:
HKD-058.e: When the deadline falls on a day off it moves to the next working day: Monday 02/11/2026.
HKD-058.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: The Q3 deadline is 31/10/2026 (Saturday) → Monday 02/11/2026.
Distractors: B doesn't shift; C is the monthly deadline; D has no basis.

HKD-059.q: The household business filing deadline for Q4/2026 is:
HKD-059.e: 31/01/2027 is a Sunday, so it moves to Monday 01/02/2027.
HKD-059.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: The Q4 deadline is 31/01/2027 (Sunday) → Monday 01/02/2027.
Distractors: B doesn't shift; C confuses it with monthly; D is the period end.

HKD-060.q: A household business with annual revenue above VND 50 billion files monthly, by the 20th of the following month.
HKD-060.e: True. Lower revenue bands file quarterly.
HKD-060.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Household businesses with revenue above 50 billion file monthly (due the 20th of the next month) – comparable to large companies; smaller groups file quarterly.

HKD-061.q: A household business with revenue not exceeding VND 1 billion that started in August 2026 notifies its 2026 revenue:
HKD-061.e: Those starting in the second half of the year notify once, by 31 January of the next year.
HKD-061.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Starting in H2 (August), the household reports revenue once, by 31/01/2027 – there was no H1 period (due 31/07).
Distractors: B applies to households operating from January; C and D are wrong.

HKD-062.q: Under Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC, household businesses notify the bank accounts used for business (form 01/BK-STK); the first deadline was 20/4/2026.
HKD-062.e: True. Bank accounts help reconcile revenue and reduce assessment risk.
HKD-062.x:
Basis: Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Household businesses notify business bank accounts on Form 01/BK-STK, first by 20/04/2026. Account data lets the authority reconcile revenue; accurate declarations reduce assessment risk.

HKD-063.q: Household businesses switching from lump-sum to self-declaration prepare an inventory list as at 31/12/2025 (form 01/BK-HTK).
HKD-063.e: True. The inventory list is the opening basis for tracking goods on transition.
HKD-063.x:
Basis: Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. On switching from presumptive tax to self-declaration, households list inventory at 31/12/2025 (Form 01/BK-HTK) – the opening balance for tracking stock and reconciling 2026 revenue and cost.

HKD-064.q: A household business files a tax return 20 days late (no mitigating factors). The fine band for organisations is VND 2–5 million, applied at the midpoint. What is the household business's fine (VND)?
HKD-064.e: Midpoint for organisations = 3.5 million; household businesses pay half = 1,750,000 VND.
HKD-064.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; Decree 310/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 20 days late – the 2–5 million band (organisations). Midpoint = 3.5 million. Household business = half → 1,750,000 VND.

HKD-065.q: A household business pays VND 50 million of tax 20 days late. What is the late payment interest (VND)?
HKD-065.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Working: 50,000,000 × 0.03% × 20 days = 300,000 VND.
Note: Interest isn't halved for households (it isn't a fine).

HKD-066.q: Late payment interest does not apply to household businesses.
HKD-066.e: False. Every late-paying taxpayer owes late payment interest of 0.03% per day.
HKD-066.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: False. Every taxpayer (enterprise, household, individual) paying late owes 0.03%/day interest – compensation for using tax money (ADM-079).

HKD-067.q: Select ALL records a household business should reconcile before filing a quarterly return:
HKD-067.e: Reconciling revenue from several sources avoids under- or double-declaration.
o: Statements of bank accounts used for business
Tax already withheld by e-commerce platforms
HKD-067.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Reconcile before filing: (A) revenue book; (B) issued e-invoices; (C) business account statements; (D) tax already withheld by e-commerce platforms (offset against the balance – HKD-103). These are exactly the authority's own cross-checks.
Distractors: (E) Shopfront photos aren't revenue data.

HKD-068.q: A household business finds last quarter's return under-declared revenue. The correct action is:
HKD-068.e: Self-correcting before an inspection avoids the incorrect-declaration penalty (late interest still applies).
o: File a supplementary return and pay the tax and late interest before the tax authority announces an inspection decision
Wait for the tax authority to find it
Add it to next quarter without a supplementary return
HKD-068.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: Amend the erroneous quarterly return and pay tax plus interest before an audit decision → no misdeclaration fine (ADM-051).
Distractors: B risks a 20% or evasion penalty; C uses the wrong period and still incurs interest; D – filed returns can't be cancelled.

HKD-069.q: A household business that properly notifies a suspension does not file tax returns during the suspension.
HKD-069.e: True. If revenue still arises during suspension, it must be declared.
HKD-069.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. A properly notified suspension means no returns during the period; if revenue still arises, it must be declared – a suspension 'on paper' doesn't remove real obligations.

HKD-070.q: Arrange the steps for a household business moving from lump-sum tax to self-declaration:
HKD-070.e: Determining the revenue band first drives the subsequent obligations.
o: Estimate annual revenue to determine the band and tax method
Notify bank accounts used for business
Register for e-invoices (if revenue exceeds VND 1 billion)
Keep revenue and expense books using the prescribed forms
Declare and pay tax by period
HKD-070.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC; Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: (1) Estimate annual revenue → group and method → (2) notify bank accounts → (3) register e-invoices if above 1 billion → (4) keep books per Circular 152/2025 → (5) file and pay periodically. Step (1) drives everything else.

HKD-071.q: The circular guiding filing documents and forms for household and individual businesses under the new policy is:
HKD-071.e: Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC (05/3/2026) issues the filing and notification forms for household and individual businesses.
HKD-071.x:
Basis: Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Circular 18/2026 (05/03/2026) sets the return, revenue-report, bank-account and inventory forms for household/individual businesses under the new policy.
Distractors: Circular 40/2021 – the old presumptive-tax rules; Circulars 200/2014 and 99/2025 are enterprise accounting regimes.

HKD-072.x:
Basis: Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Circular 18/2026/TT-BTC was issued on 05/03/2026, guiding household/individual business forms (HKD-071); the first bank account notice was due 20/04/2026 (HKD-062).

HKD-073.q: The 20% penalty on under-declared tax and the 1–3× penalty on evaded tax apply equally to household businesses and organisations, without halving.
HKD-073.e: True. The halving rule applies to fixed-amount fines; fines based on % or multiples of tax are not reduced.
HKD-073.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 'household = half of organisation' rule applies only to absolute amounts (e.g., the 2–5 million band). Percentage-based (20% misdeclaration) or multiple-based (1–3× evasion) fines apply equally.

HKD-074.q: Consider these statements on household business filing and payment deadlines:
HKD-074.e: Households not exceeding 1 billion notify revenue at most twice a year (31/7 and 31/01).
o: Monthly filing: by the 20th of the following month.
Quarterly filing: by the last day of the first month of the next quarter.
A deadline falling on a day off moves to the next working day.
Households with revenue not exceeding 1 billion notify revenue monthly.
HKD-074.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – monthly by the 20th. (2) True – quarterly by the last day of the next quarter's first month. (3) True – days off shift to the next working day. (4) False – households ≤ 1 billion report revenue at most twice a year (31/07 and 31/01).

HKD-075.q: A household business with revenue not exceeding VND 1 billion does not file quarterly tax returns.
HKD-075.e: True. Instead, it notifies revenue by the prescribed deadlines.
HKD-075.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Households ≤ 1 billion have no tax due, so no quarterly returns; they report revenue by the deadlines instead (HKD-061, ADM-063).

HKD-076.q: Late payment interest on tax is:
HKD-076.e: Late interest is not a penalty but must still be paid.
o: 0.03% per day on the late amount
HKD-076.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Interest is 0.03%/day on the late tax for every taxpayer; it isn't a penalty.
Distractors: 0.05%/day is an old rate; 0.1%/day has no basis; 20% is the misdeclaration fine.

HKD-077.q: A household business with revenue above VND 1 billion must use e-invoices (coded by the tax authority or generated from cash registers).
HKD-077.e: True. Cash-register e-invoices suit retail and food & beverage.
HKD-077.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP; Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Households above 1 billion must use e-invoices – coded by the authority or generated from cash registers; cash registers suit retail and food service with many small sales.

HKD-078.q: The deadline to register for e-invoices once cumulative revenue exceeds VND 1 billion is:
HKD-078.e: Set out in the 2026 household business policy.
o: Within 30 days from the last day of the tax period in which cumulative revenue exceeds 1 billion
Within 10 days of exceeding the threshold
By the end of the financial year
HKD-078.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Register for e-invoices within 30 days after the end of the period in which cumulative revenue exceeded 1 billion (ADM-064).
Distractors: B, C and D are wrong.

HKD-079.q: Cash-register e-invoices transmit data to the tax authority and suit retail and food & beverage businesses serving consumers.
HKD-079.e: True. Invoice data are a key revenue cross-check for the tax authority.
HKD-079.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Cash-register invoices transmit data to the authority in real time or periodically – suited to consumer retail and food service; this data is the main revenue cross-check.

HKD-080.q: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC on accounting for household and individual businesses takes effect from:
HKD-080.e: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC was issued on 31/12/2025 and took effect on 01/01/2026.
HKD-080.x:
Basis: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Circular 152/2025 on household business accounting was issued 31/12/2025 and took effect 01/01/2026 – matching the end of presumptive tax.
Distractors: B, C and D have wrong dates.

HKD-081.q: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC replaces Circular 88/2021/TT-BTC on accounting for household and individual businesses.
HKD-081.e: True. Book forms were redesigned to match the new tax policy.
HKD-081.x:
Basis: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Circular 152/2025 replaces Circular 88/2021; book formats are redesigned around the new revenue groups and tax methods (HKD-082).

HKD-082.q: Accounting book forms for household businesses under Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC are coded as:
HKD-082.e: Household businesses choose book forms by revenue band and tax method.
HKD-082.x:
Basis: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Household books are coded S1a-HKD, S2a-HKD, S2b-HKD…; the household picks formats by revenue group and method (percentage needs only a revenue book; the income method also needs cost, inventory and payroll books).
Distractors: B, C and D are enterprise book and report codes.

HKD-083.q: Accounting books and documents of household businesses must be retained for at least 5 years.
HKD-083.e: True under the household business accounting guidance.
HKD-083.x:
Basis: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Household books and documents are kept at least 5 years under the household accounting regime; e-invoices should be kept long enough for the 5-year amendment and penalty windows (ADM-003, ADM-104).

HKD-084.q: Select ALL items a household business using the income method should track in its books:
HKD-084.e: Non-business income of household members is not part of the household business books.
o: Wages and amounts payable to workers
HKD-084.x:
Basis: Circular 152/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: The income method requires tracking: (A) revenue; (B) business costs; (C) wages and employee payables; (D) stock movements.
Distractors: (E) Members' non-business income isn't in household business books.

HKD-085.q: Cash-register e-invoices do not require a digital signature on each invoice.
HKD-085.e: True. This eases high-volume retail; data are still transmitted to the tax authority.
HKD-085.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Connected cash-register invoices needn't carry a digital signature on each invoice (ADM-109), easing high-volume retail.

HKD-086.q: A household business paying VAT under the % method uses:
HKD-086.e: VAT invoices are for taxpayers using the credit method.
HKD-086.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Percentage-method (direct) taxpayers use sales invoices; VAT invoices are for credit-method taxpayers.
Distractors: B is for the credit method; C is an internal transport document; D is for fees and charges.

HKD-087.q: A household business paying at % rates may issue VAT invoices showing 10% VAT for the buyer to claim.
HKD-087.e: False. Direct-method household businesses issue sales invoices without a VAT rate.
HKD-087.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Direct-method households issue sales invoices with no VAT rate or amount; buyers can't credit input VAT from them.
Note: Business customers needing VAT invoices may prefer company suppliers – a factor in deciding whether to incorporate.

HKD-088.q: Lawful input invoices and documents are the basis for proving expenses under the income method.
HKD-088.e: True. Without invoices, expenses are disallowed.
HKD-088.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Under the income method, costs are deductible only with lawful invoices and business relevance (HKD-043); without invoices costs are disallowed, raising taxable income.

HKD-089.q: An e-invoice already sent to the buyer has an amount error. The correct treatment is:
HKD-089.e: E-invoice errors are fixed by adjustment or replacement, never deletion.
o: Issue an adjusting or replacement invoice as prescribed
Delete the invoice from the system
HKD-089.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: A sent e-invoice with the wrong amount → adjustment or replacement invoice (ADM-036).
Distractors: B – sent invoices can't be deleted (ADM-037); C – handwritten invoices are invalid; D – amount errors affect tax.

HKD-090.q: A household business with revenue not exceeding VND 1 billion may still register for e-invoices if needed (e.g., corporate customers require invoices).
HKD-090.e: True. Invoices help win organisational customers.
HKD-090.x:
Basis: Decree 254/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Households ≤ 1 billion aren't required to but may register for e-invoices when needed (corporate customers), or request per-transaction invoices (ADM-024).

HKD-091.q: An individual leasing assets with revenue above the threshold applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-091.e: 5% PIT on revenue above VND 1 billion; 5% VAT on total revenue.
HKD-091.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Leasing above the threshold: VAT 5% on full revenue; PIT 5% on revenue above 1 billion – the high PIT rate reflects leasing's low costs.
Distractors: B is services; C is food/production; D is distribution.

HKD-092.q: An individual leasing a house has revenue of VND 1.08 billion per year. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-092.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Revenue 1.08 billion > 1 billion → VAT 5% on everything: 1,080 × 5% = 54 million VND.
Note: Exceeding the threshold by only 80 million triggers VAT on the full 1.08 billion – a 'cliff effect' worth considering when pricing leases.

HKD-093.q: The same individual with leasing revenue of VND 1.08 billion per year. What PIT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-093.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: PIT = (1,080 − 1,000) × 5% = 4 million. Total tax = 54 + 4 = 58 million VND.

HKD-094.q: An individual leasing several houses applies the VND 1 billion threshold to total leasing revenue of all of them.
HKD-094.e: True. Contracts are not considered separately.
HKD-094.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 1 billion threshold uses total rental revenue across all properties, not each lease – the same principle as multiple locations (HKD-003).

HKD-095.q: When an e-commerce platform has no payment function, household businesses selling on it must declare and pay tax themselves.
HKD-095.e: True. Platforms withhold only when they have both ordering and payment functions.
HKD-095.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Platforms withhold only if they have both ordering and payment functions (ADM-014); without payment, they don't control cash, so sellers self-file.

HKD-096.q: Match each situation with who declares and pays tax:
HKD-096.e: Identifying the right filer avoids double or missed declarations.
p: E-commerce platform with ordering and payment functions
Platform withholds, declares and pays on behalf
Selling via social media, customers transfer directly
Household business declares and pays itself
Company leasing an individual's house, contract provides for proxy filing
The lessee company files and pays on behalf
HKD-096.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Platform with ordering + payment → platform withholds and files. Social-media sales with direct transfers → the household self-files (HKD-101). A company renting from an individual with a filing-on-behalf clause → the company files and pays (HKD-099).

HKD-097.q: An individual digital content creator (paid by a video-sharing platform) with revenue above the threshold applies VAT/PIT rates of:
HKD-097.e: Digital content shares the asset-leasing rate group under the 2026 household business policy.
HKD-097.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Official Letter 7403/CT-TMĐT.
Analysis: Digital content creators above the threshold use the digital content group: VAT 5% / PIT 5% (per the key) – the same rates as leasing (PIT-108).
Distractors: B is distribution; C is food/production; D is wrong above the threshold.
Note: If a foreign platform already withheld tax as required, reconcile to avoid double payment.

HKD-098.q: An individual leasing premises has revenue of VND 1.5 billion per year. What is total VAT plus PIT payable (VND million)?
HKD-098.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: VAT = 1,500 × 5% = 75 million; PIT = (1,500 − 1,000) × 5% = 25 million; total 100 million VND.

HKD-099.q: An organisation leasing assets from an individual may file and pay tax on the lessor's behalf if the contract so provides.
HKD-099.e: True. This is common when companies lease houses or offices from individuals.
HKD-099.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. An organisation renting from an individual may file and pay on their behalf if the lease says so; the tax paid is part of rent and deductible for the company's CIT (CIT-135).

HKD-100.q: Select ALL activities with a 5% PIT rate:
o: Lottery, insurance and multi-level marketing agents
HKD-100.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: 5% PIT: (A) asset leasing; (B) lottery, insurance and multi-level sales agents.
Distractors: (C) Grocery retail 0.5%; (D) food service 1.5%.

HKD-101.q: A household business selling via social media and receiving direct transfers from customers must declare this revenue itself.
HKD-101.e: True. Social media has no payment function, so no withholding occurs.
HKD-101.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Social networks lack a payment function, so no withholding; revenue received by direct transfer must be self-declared. Notified account statements (HKD-062) are the authority's cross-check.

HKD-102.q: A digital content creator has revenue of VND 1.4 billion per year. What PIT is payable at 5% (VND million)?
HKD-102.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: PIT = (1,400 − 1,000) × 5% = 20 million VND. (VAT 5% on all revenue = 70 million, if taxable.)

HKD-103.q: Revenue on which an e-commerce platform has withheld tax must still be included in the household business's total revenue to determine its band.
HKD-103.e: True. Thresholds and bands use total revenue across channels; amounts withheld are credited when computing tax still payable.
HKD-103.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The threshold and group use total revenue across all channels (store, platforms, social media); tax already withheld by platforms is offset against the balance due – avoiding both omissions and double payment.

HKD-104.q: An individual leasing warehouse space has revenue of VND 1.2 billion per year. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-104.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Warehouse rental 1.2 billion > 1 billion → VAT 5% on all: 1,200 × 5% = 60 million VND (PIT = 200 × 5% = 10 million).

HKD-105.q: A retail household has two locations: A with VND 700 million and B with 600 million revenue per year. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-105.e: Total 1,300 million > 1 billion: VAT = 1,300 × 1% = 13 million VND.
HKD-105.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Total = 700 + 600 = 1,300 million > 1 billion (though each location is below – HKD-003). VAT = 1,300 × 1% = 13 million VND.

HKD-106.q: The same household (total 1.3 billion, retail) chooses the % method. What PIT is payable (VND)?
HKD-106.e: (1,300 − 1,000) million × 0.5% = 1.5 million = 1,500,000 VND (1 billion deducted once).
HKD-106.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: PIT = (1,300 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 1.5 million VND – the 1 billion is deducted once for the household, not per location.

HKD-107.q: A household business sells goods at retail (revenue 1.2 billion) and food & beverage (0.8 billion VND), with revenue separable. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-107.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Revenue separated by group: 1,200 × 1% + 800 × 3% = 12 + 24 = 36 million VND.
Note: If not separable, 3% on all 2 billion = 60 million (HKD-028).

HKD-108.q: A beauty salon has revenue of VND 1.5 billion per year. What VAT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-108.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (per the question); the 'services, construction without materials' category.
Working: Services VAT rate 5%: 1,500 × 5% = 75 million VND.
Analysis: Pure services (beauty, hairdressing, consulting) carry the highest rate (5%) as value added is high (mainly labour). If the salon also sells cosmetics, that revenue is separated at 1%.
Note: A 2026 text – check the original.

HKD-109.q: A beauty salon with revenue of VND 1.5 billion per year chooses the % method. What PIT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-109.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: PIT = (1,500 − 1,000) × 2% = 10 million. Total tax = 75 + 10 = 85 million VND.

HKD-110.q: A household contractor doing construction without materials has revenue of VND 2 billion and chooses the % method. What is total VAT plus PIT (VND million)?
HKD-110.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Construction excluding materials: VAT = 2,000 × 5% = 100; PIT = (2,000 − 1,000) × 2% = 20; total 120 million VND.

HKD-111.q: A freight household business has revenue of VND 3 billion and chooses the % method. What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-111.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 3 billion (exactly 'not exceeding 3 billion') may still use the percentage method. PIT = (3,000 − 1,000) × 1.5% = 30 million; VAT = 3,000 × 3% = 90 million.

HKD-112.q: A restaurant has revenue of VND 2.8 billion and reasonable expenses of 2.5 billion. How much PIT (VND million) does choosing the % method save versus the income method?
HKD-112.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Percentage: (2,800 − 1,000) × 1.5% = 27 million. Income method: (2,800 − 2,500) × 15% = 45 million. The percentage method saves 45 − 27 = 18 million VND.

HKD-113.q: A retail household has revenue of VND 3 billion and reasonable expenses of 2.95 billion (very thin margin). What is PIT under the income method (15%) (VND million)?
HKD-113.e: (3,000 − 2,950) × 15% = 7.5 million, lower than the % method: (3,000 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 10 million → the income method is better.
HKD-113.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Income method: (3,000 − 2,950) × 15% = 7.5 million. Percentage: (3,000 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 10 million. The income method saves 2.5 million.
Note: Only if the 2.95 billion costs are fully documented; partial disallowance could reverse the result.

HKD-114.q: A confectionery household has revenue of VND 4 billion and reasonable expenses of 3.4 billion. What is total VAT plus PIT (VND million)?
HKD-114.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 4 billion (> 3 billion) – the income method at 17% is mandatory. VAT = 4,000 × 3% = 120; PIT = (4,000 − 3,400) × 17% = 102; total 222 million VND.

HKD-115.q: A household business pays VND 30 million of quarterly tax 15 days late. What is the late payment interest (VND)?
HKD-115.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15 (per the question) – late payment interest of 0.03% a day.
Working: Late interest = tax overdue × 0.03% × days = 30,000,000 × 0.03% × 15 = 9,000 × 15 = 135,000 VND.
Analysis: 0.03% a day ≈ 10.95% a year – above typical bank rates → don't 'borrow' from tax. Days run from the day after the deadline to the day before payment.
Check: 30,000,000 × 0.0003 = 9,000 per day ✓.

HKD-116.q: A household business has revenue of VND 80 billion and reasonable expenses of 76 billion. What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-116.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 80 billion (> 50 billion) → 20%: (80,000 − 76,000) × 20% = 800 million VND.
Note: At this scale, monthly filing applies (HKD-060); incorporation is worth considering.

HKD-117.q: An individual insurance agent earns commission of VND 1.2 billion per year. What PIT is payable (VND million)?
HKD-117.e: (1,200 − 1,000) × 5% = 10 million VND; no VAT on commission.
HKD-117.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: PIT = (1,200 − 1,000) × 5% = 10 million VND; no VAT on insurance agency commissions (HKD-033).

HKD-118.q: A household business has revenue of VND 3.8 billion and declares expenses of 3.3 billion, including 100 million of depreciation on the owner's personal car (not a transport business) and 60 million of personal spending. What is PIT (VND million)?
HKD-118.e: Deductible expenses = 3,300 − 100 − 60 = 3,140; income = 660; tax = 660 × 17% = 112.2 million VND.
HKD-118.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 3.8 billion (> 3 billion) – 17%. Deductible costs = 3,300 − 100 (owner's car depreciation – HKD-045) − 60 (personal spending) = 3,140 million. Income = 3,800 − 3,140 = 660 million; PIT = 660 × 17% = 112.2 million VND.

HKD-119.q: A retail household with revenue of VND 1.5 billion chooses the % method. What is total VAT plus PIT (VND million)?
HKD-119.x:
Basis: Decree 68/2026/ND-CP; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: VAT = 1,500 × 1% = 15 million; PIT = (1,500 − 1,000) × 0.5% = 2.5 million; total 17.5 million VND.

HKD-120.q: On inspection, the tax authority finds a household business under-declared VND 10 million of tax (not evasion). What is the incorrect-declaration penalty (VND)?
HKD-120.e: 10,000,000 × 20% = 2,000,000 VND (% fines are not halved for household businesses); late interest is added.
HKD-120.x:
Basis: Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.
Working: Misdeclaration fine = 10,000,000 × 20% = 2,000,000 VND – percentage fines aren't halved for households (HKD-073); plus the 10 million tax and interest.
